clue.text: Ruler's honest face

parts.note: straight means frank and truthful
a face or edge is a side or surface of a solid shape, as with a cliff face

explanation.surface: A monarch's frank and open countenance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruler' reads as a sovereign, but it is the drawing tool; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A straightedge is a bar with one true side used for drawing lines, which is what a ruler is.

clue.text: Bone someone you like in back of Chevy?

indicators.note: the friend sits at the rear of the vehicle, so the friend's letters come after the vehicle's

parts.note: a Chevrolet, or Chevy, is an example of a car, hence the question mark
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A suggestive invitation to get intimate with a friend in the back seat of a Chevrolet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bone' looks like a crude verb, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpal is any of the small bones of the wrist.

clue.text: Miserable place in Wales renovated completely

indicators.note: the dismal place sits inside the rebuilt letters
the word Wales is done up and rebuilt into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a hole is a squalid, dismal place to live

explanation.surface: A dreary spot in Wales has been entirely done up.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesale used as an adverb means extensively or in total, without discrimination.

clue.text: Copy part of 18

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to copy someone else's work
second meaning: 18 is NATIVITY, and the ... or manger is part of the nativity scene

explanation.walkthrough: 18 down is NATIVITY, and the manger in a nativity scene is called the crib.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to plagiarise and the manger holding the infant Jesus in a Christmas scene.

clue.text: Police officer failing hard GCSE is fired

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

indicators.note: the words hard GCSE go wrong and collapse into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; a GCSE is the British school exam taken at about sixteen

explanation.surface: A detective is sacked for flunking a tough school exam.
explanation.walkthrough: A GCSE is the British exam taken around age sixteen; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun that has been discharged has been fired, and an employee discharged has been dismissed.

clue.text: Darling dog that's partly eaten an antimacassar

definitions.note: in Peter Pan the Darling family's nursemaid is a Newfoundland dog

indicators.note: only a portion of the words eaten an antimacassar is used, the run of letters across them

parts.note: taken as written: the letters run across the end of eaten, all of an and the start of antimacassar

explanation.surface: A beloved pet that has chewed the protective cloth on the back of a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' looks like an endearment, but it is the family name from Peter Pan. An antimacassar is a cloth draped over a chair back.
explanation.definitionFit: Nana is the dog who acts as nanny to the Darling children in J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan.

clue.text: Ultimate ruin worried both sides in court

indicators.note: the worried and both sides pieces sit inside the courting word

parts.note: to woo is to court a lover
ate, as in what's eating you, means worried or troubled
right and left, R and L

explanation.surface: A final collapse troubled both parties to a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a law court but is the verb for wooing.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's final defeat gave the idiom meeting one's Waterloo, a decisive and final downfall.

clue.text: Employee often up before the board

definitions.text: Employee often up before the board
definitions.meaning: the surface pictures a worker hauled before the board of directors; the setter means a school worker standing at the blackboard

definitions.text: Employee often up before the board

explanation.walkthrough: Being up before the board sounds like a disciplinary hearing, but the board is a blackboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolteacher is an employee who spends much of the day standing at the front of the class by the blackboard.

clue.text: Kinda hot on holiday

parts.note: something hot is fashionable, or in
someone on holiday is away

explanation.surface: Fairly warm while vacationing.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinda is slang for kind of, and in a way is the equivalent hedging phrase meaning to some extent.

clue.text: Race circuit announcer retires, to dismay

indicators.note: withdrawing means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a race track
a PA is a public address system that announces things

explanation.surface: A racetrack commentator steps down, to everyone's dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to fill them with horror or consternation.

clue.text: City where you'll see German book a holiday

parts.note: Buch is German for book
taken as written
a rest is a break from work

explanation.surface: A travel tip on where to buy a German book and book a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucharest is the capital city of Romania.

clue.text: Woman cross after free hair set malfunctions

definitions.note: a singular word for a collective phrase meaning women in general

indicators.note: the cross comes after the rearranged words
the words free hair set go wrong and break into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A woman is angry when a complimentary hairdo goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective for angry, but it is the letter shaped like a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairer sex is an old-fashioned collective term for womankind.

clue.text: Current government incredibly masterful

indicators.note: the word masterful is made unbelievable, twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Today's administration is amazingly commanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective about the present government, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf Stream is a warm Atlantic ocean current flowing from the Gulf of Mexico.

clue.text: Diversion, husband going the wrong way by traffic light

parts.note: red is one of the traffic-light colours
erring means straying or going astray

explanation.surface: A detour forced on a husband who took a wrong turn at the lights.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a misleading clue that draws attention away from the truth, a distraction.

clue.text: Magazine vendor saving the covers

indicators.note: saving means except, so the word is taken without its outer letters

parts.note: a vendor is a seller

explanation.surface: A newsagent keeps the front pages of a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' looks like keeping, but it means except.
explanation.definitionFit: Elle is a well-known international fashion magazine.

clue.text: Old Peruvian laughs loudly, having secret schemes

parts.note: the Inca empire ruled ancient Peru
a hoot is a loud laugh

explanation.surface: An ancient Peruvian guffaws while plotting in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in cahoots is to be in secret partnership or conspiracy with someone.

clue.text: Complicated taste was prominent

parts.note: a tang is a sharp distinctive flavour
to have led is to have been out in front

explanation.surface: An intricate flavour dominated the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tangled is knotted and intricate, hence complex and hard to sort out.

clue.text: New York hosts busy accommodating four for Christmas

indicators.note: the city's letters take in a guest between them
the busy phrase makes room inside for the numeral

parts.note: at it means hard at work
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A busy New York takes in four guests over the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nativity is the birth of Jesus, celebrated as Christmas.

clue.text: Slow boat departed with mixed load for the east

indicators.note: the mixed letters stand in for the east, replacing it

parts.note: gone means left or departed
E is the compass abbreviation for east
the letters of load stirred into a new order, a jumbled load

explanation.surface: A sluggish vessel left with a jumbled cargo bound eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the east' reads as a destination, but it says the mixed letters replace the E.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola is the leisurely flat-bottomed rowing boat of the Venetian canals.

clue.text: Job, Simpson's first away from Springfield?

indicators.note: the letter is taken out of the singer's first name

parts.note: Dusty Springfield was a British pop singer

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the name Simpson is used

parts.note: taken as written; the name supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: A question about the role of the first Simpson to leave the cartoon town of Springfield.
explanation.walkthrough: Springfield suggests the Simpsons' home town, but it is the singer Dusty Springfield.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty is a task or responsibility one is required to carry out.

clue.text: Heavy metal fan ate sausage sandwiches back in queue

indicators.note: the eating and sausage words enclose the letter like bread round a filling

parts.note: had, as in had dinner, means ate

indicators.note: only the last letter of queue is taken

parts.note: taken as written; its final letter is used
banger is British slang for a sausage

explanation.surface: A rocker eats a sausage sandwich while standing in line.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A headbanger is a fan of heavy metal music who shakes his or her head violently to the beat.

clue.text: Bird shot dead by comedian

parts.note: a go or a shot is an attempt
a wit is someone clever and funny

explanation.surface: A bird is gunned down by a comic.
explanation.definitionFit: The godwit is a long-billed wading bird of the sandpiper family.

clue.text: Try to catch Pedro illicitly trapping birds

indicators.note: the rearranged name closes round the birds
the name Pedro is treated improperly, its letters set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Aves is the scientific class name for birds

explanation.surface: Pedro is caught poaching birds.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen secretly, trying to overhear a private conversation.

clue.text: Very large egg for one person

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
an egg is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A huge egg serves just one diner.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo performance or meal is undertaken alone, by a single individual.

clue.text: Old man will lose vitality

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
the contraction 'll stands for will

explanation.surface: Father will become feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: To pall is to become less appealing or interesting, losing freshness through familiarity.

clue.text: More vintage wine left over, to be returned

indicators.note: sent back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: red is red wine
O is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A leftover vintage red that's going back to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: O for over is the cricket scoring abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Vintage things are of a past era, so something more vintage is of greater age.

clue.text: Part of pistol engineer knocked off

indicators.note: only a section running across the words pistol engineer is used

parts.note: taken as written: the letters straddle the end of pistol and the start of engineer

explanation.surface: A piece of a gun engineer's work was taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocked off is slang for taken illegally, a sense of pinched or nicked.

clue.text: Don't fuss about mud brought back into shelter

indicators.note: the reversed mud goes inside the sheltering word

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

indicators.note: fetched in the opposite direction, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: dirt is mud or grime

explanation.surface: Telling someone not to worry about dirt being trodden indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To let something ride is to take no action over it and let it pass.
